title: What React solves and its boundaries
runtime: React 19.3 learning project with a current Vite setup. Version-specific commands must be checked against the linked React, Vite, and npm pages before use.

objectives.text: Explain the UI problem React is designed to solve.
Describe what React provides and what React DOM provides.
Name important problems React alone does not solve.

diagnostic.question: What problem does what react solves and its boundaries help you solve?
diagnostic.answer: Name the relevant layer, its input and output, and one problem it does not solve.

sections.title: React manages changing user interfaces
sections.body: React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces from components. You describe what the interface should look like for the current data, and React keeps the browser DOM in step when that data changes. This is useful when a page has many connected states and reusable pieces. A static article with almost no interaction may not need React.

sections.title: React and React DOM have different jobs
sections.body: The react package contains the component and state model. react-dom connects that model to browser DOM nodes. A web entry file usually imports createRoot from react-dom/client and renders an App component. React can also target other environments through other renderers, so React itself is not the browser or a complete website server.

sections.title: React is one layer
sections.body: React does not choose your URL routing, database, authentication, API design, deployment platform, or full styling approach. A client-only build tool also does not automatically provide server rendering, data loading, or production architecture. These choices come from a framework, other libraries, platform code, or your own design.

sections.title: Choose from the product need
sections.body: Use plain HTML and JavaScript when the page is small and the platform is enough. Add a React root to an existing page when one region needs component state. A Vite React project is useful for learning or a client-only app. React recommends a framework for many new production apps because a framework can coordinate routing, data, rendering, and deployment concerns.

sections.title: Use evidence instead of setup guesses
sections.body: When setup fails, identify the layer before changing code. Read the terminal command and first error, confirm the current directory and versions, check the browser Network and Console, and trace the entry file to the root component. Make one small correction, rerun the same check, and record what proved the fix.

interviewQuestions.question: What responsibility does what react solves and its boundaries have in a React project?
interviewQuestions.answer: Explain the UI problem React is designed to solve. Describe what React provides and what React DOM provides. Name important problems React alone does not solve. Choose between no React, gradual React, a build tool, and a framework.
interviewQuestions.followUp: What important responsibility belongs to another layer?

interviewQuestions.question: How would you debug a failure related to what react solves and its boundaries?
interviewQuestions.answer: Reproduce the smallest failure, confirm the current directory and versions when relevant, read the first terminal or browser error, trace the entry and root, and test one hypothesis at a time.
interviewQuestions.followUp: Which evidence would make you change layers?

interviewQuestions.question: Which tradeoff in what react solves and its boundaries should a team decide explicitly?
interviewQuestions.answer: The team should match tools and boundaries to product needs, record version and deployment assumptions, and avoid treating a starter template as a complete production architecture.
interviewQuestions.followUp: How could the answer change for an existing server-rendered site?

commonMistakes.symptom: Every setup problem is described as a React error.
commonMistakes.cause: Browser, Node, npm, Vite, project files, and React responsibilities were mixed together.
commonMistakes.fix: Identify the failing layer from the command, URL, stack, file, or tool panel before editing.

commonMistakes.symptom: Commands work in one terminal but fail in another folder.
commonMistakes.cause: The current directory or active Node installation differs.
commonMistakes.fix: Check the path, package.json, lockfile, node -v, and npm -v in the same terminal.

commonMistakes.symptom: The starter template is treated as a complete production plan.
commonMistakes.cause: Scaffolding and build features were confused with routing, data, server, security, and deployment architecture.
commonMistakes.fix: Write product requirements and assign each responsibility to React, a build tool, a framework, the platform, or backend code.

publicationChecklist.note: Concept-complete setup draft. Recheck version-specific commands, run broader browser behavior checks, obtain independent review, and complete a learner trial before publication.
